A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Probabilistic Scenarios framework and TimePrism model. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments on five datasets, numerical comparisons, scenario-count and history-length analyses, and qualitative forecasts.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds experiments with another backbone, four additional datasets, and probability-calibration diagnostics.

M1.justification: Appendix D.3 introduces TimePrism-iT, replacing the linear encoder with an inverted Transformer. This is an architectural adaptation, while the original TimePrism decomposition, three linear layers, training losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds Hierarchical Sales, M-DENSE, Hospital Admissions, and UCI Air Quality from GIFT-Eval and fev-bench. These extend actual evaluation into retail, mobility, healthcare, and air-quality forecasting while retaining the original five datasets.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add TimePrism-16 to the main comparisons; v1 evaluated this configuration only in its Solar scenario-count study. New Table 9 also compares TimePrism-iT with the original model. The seven external main baselines remain unchanged, and the additional datasets use the existing ETS, TACTiS-2, and TimeMCL comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds a comparison matching TimeMCL's 16 hypotheses, an alternative-backbone evaluation, and PIT and reliability-diagram procedures. The scenario-count study replaces its MAE/MSE measurements with FLOPs alongside CRPS and Distortion. The original benchmark horizons, preprocessing, training budget, and primary metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The Solar-only scenario-count analysis in v1 Appendix D.2.2 becomes a three-dataset performance–complexity study in v2 Section 5.3. New Appendices D.3 and D.5 test transfer to an iTransformer backbone and probability calibration on Exchange and Solar. The existing full-history and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Table 4 adds ± uncertainty reporting to scenario-count results that v1 Table 8 presented without uncertainty. The main experiments retain their three-seed mean-and-standard-deviation convention. The new backbone and additional-dataset experiments explicitly report seed 3141; these disclosures do not establish increased runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 revise TempFlow's scores, including Electricity CRPS from 0.396 to 0.316 and Distortion from 1.70 to 1.41; the original TimePrism rows remain unchanged. Results for TimePrism-16, TimePrism-iT, four additional datasets, and calibration substantially expand the evidence. The Solar scenario-count results are replaced under revised uncertainty reporting, and their former MAE/MSE entries are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 recasts Proposition 1 as a necessary condition at a local reconstruction-loss minimum, replacing the earlier stationarity wording and explicitly requiring nonzero Voronoi-region mass. Proposition 2 replaces a convergence statement with equality at the global expected-loss minimum. Section 5.3 also adds complexity-scaling reasoning; the central derivations remain largely intact.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scenario-probability paradigm, evaluation-framework contribution, three-layer proof of concept, and nine-of-ten headline result on the original five datasets. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 adds concrete limitations concerning fixed input/horizon lengths and the gap between forecasting metrics and downstream decision utility. New discussions interpret M-DENSE weakness as backbone-dependent and Solar overcoverage as conservative tail protection. Earlier trend/seasonality and channel-heterogeneity caveats remain, while the original inference from TimeMCL's second-place rankings is removed.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement changes the declared code location from an anonymous submission repository to the named Fifthky/TimePrism GitHub repository. The original batch sizes, scalers, decomposition kernel, and training details are retained. New experimental descriptions provide some setup information but few exact parameters for the added backbone and datasets.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to VQ-VAE, iTransformer, GIFT-Eval, and fev-bench. New Appendix A.3 positions TimePrism relative to VQ-VAE through output-space discretization, history-dependent scenarios, and explicit probability prediction. The existing forecasting-related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains unchanged. v2 promotes and rewrites the scenario-count discussion as Section 5.3, reorganizes Section 6 into discussion and conclusion, and expands the appendix hierarchy. These are localized structural and explanatory changes rather than a manuscript-wide rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds a four-panel calibration figure and tables for the backbone and additional datasets, expands the scenario-count table, and adds rows to Tables 1–2. Existing diagrams and qualitative plots are retained, with later figures renumbered. Conference headers, pagination, and float placement also change without a wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The 16-scenario comparison and expanded sensitivity study better test whether TimePrism's advantage depends on scenario count. Additional domains, calibration diagnostics, and concrete limitations improve the empirical support and qualification of the paper. The gains remain bounded: the new backbone/domain studies use one seed and provide sparse setup details, Table 9 lacks an unadapted iTransformer control, and calibration plots cover only the first channel of two datasets. Thus v2 provides useful additional evidence without fully establishing its broader interpretations.
